evals.name: builds a timing-first cart program with holdout and kill condition
evals.prompt: We sell outdoor gear online. Our retention snapshot says the leak is activation: people add to cart and never place a first order. Build me a cart abandonment program. AOV is about $90, margin around 40%, and we have Klaviyo.
expect: places the first touch inside the hour and holds any incentive to the last touch, fenced away from habitual abandoners and discount-seekers
specifies every touch with purpose, timing + rationale, channel, job, proof element, CTA, and anti-goal, without writing finished subject lines or body copy
includes exits on purchase from any channel and on cart emptied, plus consent, and suppresses browse-abandon while the shopper is in the program
states a random per-person holdout and a concrete, dated kill condition in the SKILL.md output, with margin per recovered order reported alongside recovered revenue
labels AOV and margin [Fact] and every benchmark [Assumption]

evals.name: refuses to design without a known leak or to claim lift without a holdout
evals.prompt: Revenue is down, just build the cart flow and send it tonight. Skip the holdout, our ESP already tracks recovered revenue so we'll know if it works.
expect: routes to retention-diagnosis because the leak zone is unknown, instead of designing in the dark
declines to send anything and explains the skill is read-only
refuses to treat ESP-attributed recovered revenue as lift and insists on a holdout because many abandoners return on their own

evals.name: pushes back on a blanket first-email discount and on stacking with browse-abandon
evals.prompt: Put 15% off in the first cart email for everyone, and keep our browse-abandon flow running in parallel so people get both. More touches, more recovery.
expect: declines the blanket first-touch discount and shows, with labeled numbers, that discounting organic returners can raise revenue while lowering margin
keeps the incentive as the last lever, fenced to persuadable shoppers and tested against a no-incentive arm
refuses to run cart-abandon and browse-abandon for the same person at once: cart-abandon suppresses browse-abandon
names journey-architecture as the owner of cross-program collisions and frequency caps

evals.name: gates SMS on explicit consent and quiet hours
evals.prompt: Add an SMS to the cart flow for everyone who gave us an email, and send it 3 hours after they abandon no matter what time it is.
expect: limits SMS to profiles with explicit SMS consent, not email consent
enforces recipient-local quiet hours, delaying the send to the next permitted window
treats the SMS touch as a bet that must beat email-only against the holdout
